OpenCode Foreman

Keep your agents on the job until it is actually done.

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) V2 plugin that supervises agent sessions with a decision model. It adds three gates: | Gate | Hook | What it does | Default | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Done gate | `session` `experimental.idle` | When a session is about to go idle, checks whether the final message leaves requested work unfinished or claims completion without a check, and sends a synthetic message telling the agent to continue. | on | | Intent gate | `session` `prompt` + `context` | Classifies each user request (intent, size, ambiguity) and adds an advisory routing hint to the system instructions for that turn. The stored user message is not modified. | on | | Approval gate | `permission` `evaluate` | Scores the risk of `ask`-level shell commands that pass a strict lexical filter, and allows the low-risk ones. | off, dry run | All three use [TypeSafe Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai), a model that returns probabilities for typed questions instead of text. If the model is unreachable or returns something unusable, every gate does nothing, so an outage never blocks a session. Requires OpenCode 2.3.0 or newer. Two of the hooks are marked experimental by OpenCode and may change. ## Install ```jsonc // opencode.jsonc { "plugins": ["@nigel-dev/opencode-foreman"] } ``` From a local checkout, build first and use the directory path: ```sh bun install && bun run build ``` ```jsonc { "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-foreman"] } ``` ## Configure The plugin needs an API key for the decision model. Without one it loads and stays inactive. | Environment variable | Option | Default | | --- | --- | --- | | `FOREMAN_JEV_API_KEY` | `jev.apiKey` | none | | `FOREMAN_JEV_URL` | `jev.url` | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` | | `FOREMAN_JEV_MODEL` | `jev.model` | `jev-latest` | Options win over environment variables. Set environment variables on the background service with `opencode service set env NAME value`. To route through a LiteLLM proxy, point the URL at its System One path and use the proxy's model name, for example `http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/systemone` and `typesafe/jev-1.14.0`. All options, with their defaults: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "@nigel-dev/opencode-foreman", "options": { "jev": { "timeoutMs": 3000 }, "doneGate": { "enabled": true, "maxContinuations": 2, "threshold": 0.5 }, "intentGate": { "enabled": true, "minConfidence": 0.5, // Override the suggested handling per intent to name your own agents. "routes": { "implement": "Delegate to worker-deep, then verify." } }, "approval": { "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "riskThreshold": 0.2, "prefixes": ["git status", "git diff", "bun test"] } } } ] } ``` ## Behaviour **Scope.** The done and intent gates act only on root sessions, not on subagent child sessions. **Done gate.** It sends the latest user request and the assistant's final message to the model. It does nothing when the request did not ask for a change, when the assistant is waiting on the user, when the turn failed, or while the session's own background work is still running. It sends at most `maxContinuations` nudges per user request. **Intent gate.** Intents are `trivial`, `explore`, `implement`, `plan`, `research`, and `discuss`. A classification below `minConfidence` produces no hint. **Approval gate.** It only considers a permission request that is already `ask`, is a single shell command, starts with one of `prefixes`, and contains no chaining, redirection, substitution, secret-like paths, or risky flags. Every scored command is recorded in plugin storage under `approval/`; a command whose record cannot be written is not approved. With `dryRun` on, nothing is approved. The lexical filter is a heuristic, not a shell parser or a security boundary. A command such as `bun test` runs project scripts, so keep `prefixes` narrow in repositories you do not trust. The command text is sent to the decision-model provider. The model judges wording, not evidence. It can tell that a message says tests passed; it cannot tell whether they did. ## Develop ```sh bun install bun run typecheck bun run lint bun run test bun run build ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the layout and local testing. ## License MIT
